sense: to a greater degree: more beautiful, love more

terms.gloss: the comparative: dearer, more beautiful, faster
terms.grammar: the comparative degree of an adjective or adverb (cārior, citius), with quam or the ablative of the thing compared
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.3.5: mihi tē cārius nihil esse
Lewis & Short s.v. comparātīvus: gradus, the comparative (Donatus)
terms.comment: Latin says “more” with the ending: cārior, dearer; citius, faster. “Than” is quam, or the ablative of what is compared: plūs oculīs meīs (Catull. 14.1). “Much more” is multō with the comparative, “a little more” paulō (see a lot, a little).

evidence: Sen. Ep. 78.22: magis juvat bibere sitientem
Publil. Sent. N 35: Nīl magis amat cupiditās, quam quod nōn licet.
terms.comment: With verbs, and with adjectives that make no comparative, most of them with a vowel before the ending (idōneus, necessārius): magis idōneus, better suited; magis … quam, more than, rather than (Vulg. Act. 20.35).

terms.gloss: more (with verbs: love more, be worth more)
evidence: Catull. 14.1: nī tē plūs oculīs meīs amārem
Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō
terms.comment: “Love more” is plūs amāre. For “more” of a thing, see more. Classical prose does not put plūs with an adjective: “more suitable” is magis idōneus.

phrases.latin: nī tē plūs oculīs meīs amārem
phrases.english: if I didn’t love you more than my own eyes

phrases.latin: nōn enim concēdō tibi plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō
phrases.english: for I don’t grant that you love him more than I do

phrases.latin: magis juvat bibere sitientem, grātior est ēsurientī cibus
phrases.english: drink gives more pleasure to the thirsty, and food is more welcome to the hungry

phrases.latin: Nīl magis amat cupiditās, quam quod nōn licet.
phrases.english: Desire loves nothing more than what is not allowed.

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās et ita tibi persuādeās, mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse
phrases.english: look after your health, and be sure that nothing is or ever was dearer to me than you

phrases.latin: Beātius est magis dare, quam accipere.
phrases.english: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

phrases.latin: tempus hoc magis idōneum quam umquam anteā
phrases.english: this time, better suited than ever before

phrases.latin: nūllum enim officium referendā grātiā magis necessārium est
phrases.english: for no duty is more necessary than returning a kindness

phrases.latin: Tibi, pater, permittimus: plūs scīs quid factō opus est.
phrases.english: We leave it to you, father: you know better what needs doing.

phrases.latin: quem quī audiunt intellegere etiam et sapere plūs quam cēterōs arbitrantur
phrases.english: those who hear him think he understands and knows more than the rest

phrases.latin: Cēnset sē plūs sapere quam mē.
phrases.english: He thinks he knows better than I do.
